questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Elements 'X' and 'Y' are the most and least electronegative elements, respectively among N, As, Sb and P. The nature of the oxides $\mathrm{X_2O_3}$ and $\mathrm{Y_2O_3}$ is acidic and amphoteric, respectively.
Statement II: $\mathrm{BCl_3}$ is covalent in nature and gets hydrolysed in water. It produces $\mathrm{[B(OH)_4]^-}$ and $\mathrm{[B(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ in aqueous medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{N > P > As > Sb}$ (N: most EN; Sb: least EN)
$\mathrm{X = N}$, $\mathrm{X_2O_3 = N_2O_3}$ (Acidic)
$\mathrm{Y = Sb}$, $\mathrm{Y_2O_3 = Sb_2O_3}$ (Amphoteric)
$\mathrm{BCl_3 + 3H_2O \rightarrow B(OH)_3 + 3HCl}$
So, Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.stem:
At T(K), 100 g of 98% $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (w/w) aqueous solution is mixed with 100 g of 49% $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (w/w) aqueous solution. What is the mole fraction of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the resultant solution?
(Given : Atomic mass H = 1u; S = 32u; O = 16u).
(Assume that temperature after mixing remains constant)
questions.solution:
Total wt. of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4} = \left(100 \times \frac{98}{100}\right) + \left(100 \times \frac{49}{100}\right) = 147\ \mathrm{g}$
Total wt. of $\mathrm{H_2O} = 200 - 147 = 53\ \mathrm{g}$
$$\text{mole fraction of } \mathrm{H_2SO_4} = \frac{\frac{147}{98}}{\left(\frac{147}{98} + \frac{53}{18}\right)} = 0.337$$

questions.stem: The energy of first (lowest) Balmer line of H atom is $x$ J. The energy (in J) of second Balmer line of H atom is :
questions.solution:
$n_1 = 2, n_2 = 3$ ($\mathrm{I^{st}}$ Balmer Line)
$$\Delta E = x = 13.6(1)^{2}\left(\frac{1}{2^{2}} - \frac{1}{3^{2}}\right) \quad \ldots(\mathrm{I})$$
$n_1 = 2, n_2 = 4$ ($\mathrm{2^{nd}}$ Balmer Line)
$$\Delta E = 13.6(1^{2})\left[\frac{1}{2^{2}} - \frac{1}{4^{2}}\right] \quad \ldots(\mathrm{II})$$
$$\frac{(\mathrm{II})}{(\mathrm{I})} = \frac{\Delta E}{x} = \frac{\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16}}{\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}} = \frac{27}{20}$$
$(\Delta E = 1.35x)$

B. At a given temperature, lower the $E_a$, faster is the reaction.

Consider the following electrochemical cell : $\mathrm{Pt\,|\,O_2(g)(1\,bar)\,|\,HCl(aq)\,||\,M^{2+}(aq, 1.0\,M)\,|\,M(s)}$
The pH above which, oxygen gas would start to evolve at anode is ______ (nearest integer).
[Given: $E^\circ_{\mathrm{M^{2+}/M}} = 0.994\ \mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ_{\mathrm{O_2/H_2O}} = 1.23\ \mathrm{V}$ } standard reduction potential
and $\frac{RT}{F}(2.303) = 0.059\ \mathrm{V}$ at the given condition]

$$\mathrm{H_2O \rightarrow 2H^+ + \frac{1}{2}O_2 + 2e^-}$$

$-0.097 = -1.23 + 0.059 \times \mathrm{pH}$
$\mathrm{pH} = 3.94 \approx 4$

questions.stem: If the enthalpy of sublimation of Li is $155\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, enthalpy of dissociation of $\mathrm{F_2}$ is $150\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, ionization enthalpy of Li is $520\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, electron gain enthalpy of F is $-313\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, standard enthalpy of formation of LiF is $-594\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. The magnitude of lattice enthalpy of LiF is ______ $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
Born-Haber cycle: $\mathrm{Li(s) + \frac{1}{2}F_2(g) \xrightarrow{-617} LiF(s)}$; $\mathrm{Li(s) \xrightarrow{155\ kJ} Li(g) \xrightarrow{520\ kJ} Li^+(g)}$; $\mathrm{\frac{1}{2}F_2(g) \xrightarrow{150/2} F(g) \xrightarrow{-313\ kJ} F^-(g)}$; $\mathrm{Li^+(g) + F^-(g) \xrightarrow{L.E.} LiF(s)}$
$$-594 = 155 + 520 + \frac{150}{2} - 313 + \mathrm{L.E.}$$
$\mathrm{L.E.} = -1031\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$
